_README: Translation units the C++ analysers are EXPECTED not to build, and why.
A file that does not compile contributes no findings and looks, in every
total the sweep prints, exactly like a file that is clean. The C tier's
tools/verify/expected_errors.py exists because libexec/rtld-elf/rtld.c did
that on an unresolvable #include and the defect behind it cost thirty-seven
boot runs. This is the same inventory for C++.
Anything erroring that is NOT here is a NEW hole. Anything here that
compiles now is a STALE exemption. Both are reported by
cxx_analyze.py --check-errors   and   cxx_tidy.py --check-errors
'prefixes' absorb a subtree. They are used for KDE ONLY, and each one
carries the count it absorbed when it was written, so the scale of the
exemption is on the page rather than implied. A prefix is a WEAKER record
than a file entry: it will absorb a genuinely new failure inside that
project without saying so. It is used here because the alternative is
1,386 identical entries, and it should be replaced with file entries as
soon as the Qt6 dependencies make the number small.
'files' are per-file and carry the actual first error.
PROVENANCE: generated from run_kde.jsonl (1,392 TUs: 6 OK, 1,386 ERROR)
and run_hbsd_own.jsonl (263 TUs: 113 OK, 141 ERROR, 9 TIMEOUT),
clang 18.1.3, 2026-09-17, in a container with no Qt and no FreeBSD
headers. Several hbsd entries -- sys/_types.h, fpmath.h, machine/float.h,
namespace.h -- are CONTAINER artefacts: they are FreeBSD headers being
asked for on a Linux host and they will NOT occur on the user's machine.
Those entries are expected to go stale and --check-errors is expected to
say so. That is the mechanism working, not a defect.
